cards.text: The prophet Micah just painted a gorgeous future: nations beating their swords into plowshares, nobody training for war anymore (Micah 4:3). Then he turns to Jerusalem, the Daughter of Zion, and talks about RIGHT NOW. Right now she's crying out loud, and Micah asks her why: is there no king among you, has your counselor perished?

cards.question: Micah says anguish is gripping the Daughter of Zion. What does he say she's like?

cards.text: Micah doesn't say calm down, friend. He says go ahead and WRITHE like a woman in labor, because she's about to leave the city and camp out in the open fields.

cards.question: Micah says the Daughter of Zion will leave the city, camp in the open fields and go to ___.
True or false: Micah says Babylon is where the LORD will redeem the Daughter of Zion from the hand of her enemies.

cards.text: I got rescued out of the back of a JUNK DRAWER, friend, so Babylon? The LORD's got it. But right now, many nations have assembled against Zion, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let us feast our eyes on Zion.”

cards.question: Many nations have gathered against Zion, ready to stare her down. Who does Micah say actually gathered them there?

cards.text: The nations don't know the LORD's thoughts or understand His plan, because He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor. They came to stare at Zion, but friend, they're the ones being gathered like the HARVEST.

cards.question: The nations are gathered like sheaves on the threshing floor. What does Micah tell the Daughter of Zion to do?

cards.text: And she gets the gear for the job: horns of iron and hooves of bronze to break many peoples to pieces. Zion shows up to this harvest built like a TANK.

cards.question: True or false: Micah says the Daughter of Zion will keep the wealth of those peoples for herself.

cards.text: Then Micah snaps right back to NOW. A siege is laid against us, he says, so mobilize your troops.

cards.question: True or false: with a siege laid against them, Micah says the judge of Israel will be struck on the cheek with a rod.

cards.text: Then the message turns to a little town, small among the clans of Judah. Out of it will come One to be ruler over Israel, which is like the tiniest bakery on the block landing the ROYAL order.

cards.question: Which small town in Judah will this ruler over Israel come from?
True or false: Micah says the origins of the ruler from Bethlehem go back to the days of eternity.

cards.text: Fast forward to Matthew: magi from the east show up asking where the King of the Jews was born, and the chief priests and scribes point King Herod straight to this verse. Jesus was born right there in Bethlehem of Judea (Matthew 2:1-6).
Back in Micah, Israel will be abandoned until she who is in labor has given birth. There's that labor picture again.

cards.question: True or false: once she who is in labor gives birth, Micah says the rest of the ruler's brothers will return to the children of Israel.

cards.text: No corner office for this ruler. He will stand and shepherd His flock.

cards.question: True or false: Micah says the ruler from Bethlehem will shepherd His flock in His own strength, without the LORD.
With the ruler from Bethlehem shepherding the flock, how does Micah say His people will live?

cards.text: His greatness will reach to the ends of the earth, friend, the WHOLE map. Then Micah names a real threat: Assyria, whose king captured Samaria (2 Kings 17:6), invading the land and trampling its citadels.

cards.question: When Assyria invades and tramples their citadels, Micah says the ruler from Bethlehem will be our ___.

cards.text: Against Assyria, they'll raise up seven shepherds, even eight leaders of men. EIGHT leaders? I've been begging for helpers in this bakery, and Micah's got a whole ROSTER!

cards.question: Seven shepherds and eight leaders rise up against Assyria. What does Micah say they'll do to its land?

cards.text: They'll rule Assyria, the land of Nimrod, the mighty hunter who went into Assyria and built Nineveh (Genesis 10:8-11). And Micah wraps it up: He will deliver us when Assyria marches into our borders.

findings.problem: The story card is three sentences: "I got rescued out of the back of a JUNK DRAWER, friend, so Babylon?", "The LORD's got it." and "But right now, many nations have assembled against Zion..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Zion shows up to this harvest built like a TANK" puts the tank comparison inside the Bible's harvest scene. It blends the comparison with the Bible setting instead of using one image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The whole card is about Matthew 2:1-6. It tells no part of Micah 4:9-5:6 and does not move the baker forward through the passage. It also crowds several beats into two sentences: the magi asking, the priests and scribes answering Herod, and Jesus born in Bethlehem. Outside facts are allowed only when they help a card that is telling the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The story card is three sentences: "Against Assyria, they'll raise up...", "EIGHT leaders?" and "I've been begging for helpers..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Micah 5:5 says "We will raise against it seven shepherds." The card changes the speaker to "they'll raise up," which changes who does the raising.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Seven shepherds and eight leaders rise up" turns the text's single phrase "seven shepherds, even eight leaders of men" (Micah 5:5) into two separate groups. The text does not say that.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "They'll rule Assyria, the land of Nimrod" says Assyria is the land of Nimrod. Micah 5:6 names the land of Assyria and the land of Nimrod side by side and leaves open how they connect. Genesis 10:10-11 places the start of Nimrod's kingdom in Shinar, from which he went into Assyria.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The walkthrough is light on real laughs. Many story cards are plain retelling with no reaction, disbelief or self-deprecation (stop 1 cards 3, 8 and 12; stop 2 cards 5, 10 and 14). The jokes that are there are mild: "No corner office for this ruler," "the tiniest bakery on the block landing the ROYAL order" and "built like a TANK." They read as pleasant rather than laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
